name: validation/schemas
about: Which schemas a runtime accepts, and what the text it accepts means. A schema one runtime loads and another refuses splits a fleet at deploy time; one both load but read differently gives the two servers different hashes for the same file, so neither recognises the other's clients. Every rejection sits beside a guard that differs from it only in the rule under test and must load, so a runtime that refuses too much fails as surely as one that refuses too little.
source: spec 01 §1 (lexical structure), §3 (types), §4 (@input, @http(name:)), §7 (reserved names) and §8 (validation rules). The diagnostic codes runtimes print are not in the specification, so a case pins only whether the schema is valid; the guard beside it is what makes the rejection about the rule it names.
rule: A case is `expect: "rejected"` (loading fails: the text does not parse, or the IR breaks a rule of §8) or `expect: "accepted"` (it parses and validates, warnings allowed).

`schema` is `.rayfold` text. `irEdit` then edits the IR document that text parses to (unvalidated) before validating it: `path` is a list of member names and array indexes into the document of §9, and `value` replaces what is there. That is how a case states an IR no text can produce - an importer, a builder or a lock file can write a name the lexer cannot read, and §1 applies to it all the same.

An accepted case may carry `irHas`: members of its IR document (path as above) and the value each must hold. An accepted case may carry `sameAs`: the name of another accepted case whose schema must have the same schema hash, so two spellings of one schema are one identity.
A type parameter is in scope only in the fields of the generic that declares it (§3, §6); `Page<T>` is an object, so it is a result type and never an argument or input field (§8.3).
`@input(Type)` takes a type a client can send: an input, scalar or enum (§4, §8.3).

Within one owner no member is named twice: fields of a type, arguments of an operation or field, values of an enum, members of a union (§8.1). The text parser refuses the first three on its own, so each also has a case in IR form, which reaches validation without a parser.
A name is `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*`, and one starting with `__` or `$` is reserved, for types, fields, arguments, operations and enum values alike, whatever produced the IR (§1, §7, §8.12).

`@http(name:)` is written only on operation arguments and input fields, with `name` as its one argument and a non-empty string; within one operation's arguments or one input type's fields, no wire name equals another member's name or wire name (§4, §8.11).

A block string's one escape is `\"""`, standing for `"""`; the text is dedented and trimmed, and `\r\n` is a line break (§1). An object key that is not a name is quoted, and a quoted key that is a name is the same key (§1).

cases.name: a type parameter outside a generic
cases.schema:
entity Book { id: ID x: T }
query book(id: ID): Book?
cases.why: T names nothing here; a runtime that let type parameters resolve anywhere accepted it

cases.name: guard: the built-in generic uses its own parameter
cases.schema:
entity Book { id: ID }
query books(page: PageArgs): Page<Book>

cases.name: Page<T> as an operation argument
cases.schema:
entity Book { id: ID }
query book(id: ID, p: Page<String>): Book?
cases.why: an argument is something a client sends, and Page is an object; the generic branch used to return before the position was checked. A page of strings, so the type argument is one an argument may hold and only the position of Page itself is wrong

cases.name: guard: PageArgs as an operation argument
cases.schema:
entity Book { id: ID }
query book(id: ID, p: PageArgs): Book?

cases.name: Page<T> as an input field
cases.why: a page of strings, in a list: the element type is one an input may hold and the rule that a page field takes page arguments does not apply, so only the position of Page itself is wrong

cases.name: guard: PageArgs as an input field
@input with a value that is not a type, in an IR
cases.why: text cannot write this (the parser reads a type there), but a builder or importer can write the name as a string; the value must be a type reference

cases.name: @input naming a type a client cannot send
guard: @input naming an input type
a field named twice
cases.schema:
entity Book { id: ID title: String title: String }
query book(id: ID): Book?
cases.why: the IR keeps both, and which one a result carries would be whichever an implementation happened to read last

cases.name: an input field named twice
an argument named twice
cases.schema:
entity Book { id: ID }
query book(id: ID, id: ID): Book?

cases.name: an enum value named twice
a union member named twice
a field named twice, in an IR
cases.schema:
entity Book { id: ID title: String subtitle: String }
query book(id: ID): Book?
cases.why: the parser refuses the text form above; an IR from an importer, the builder or a lock file reaches validation without it

cases.name: an input field named twice, in an IR
an argument named twice, in an IR
cases.schema:
entity Book { id: ID }
query book(id: ID, q: ID): Book?

cases.name: an enum value named twice, in an IR
guard: every member named once
guard: the same edits with names the owner does not have
an argument name starting with __
cases.schema:
entity Book { id: ID }
query book(id: ID, __x: Int): Book?

cases.name: an enum value starting with __
a field name starting with __
cases.schema:
entity Book { id: ID __x: Int }
query book(id: ID): Book?

cases.name: guard: one leading underscore is an ordinary name
a field named $type in an IR
cases.schema:
entity Book { id: ID title: String }
query book(id: ID): Book?
cases.why: $type is the member every result uses to say what an object is; a field of that name would overwrite it

cases.name: a field name no schema file could hold, in an IR
cases.schema:
entity Book { id: ID title: String }
query book(id: ID): Book?
cases.why: an importer or a builder writes IR directly; a name the lexer cannot read back makes a schema no file can print

cases.name: an argument name no schema file could hold, in an IR
cases.schema:
entity Book { id: ID }
query book(id: ID, q: String): Book?

cases.name: an enum value no schema file could hold, in an IR
guard: the same edit with a name the lexer reads
cases.why: the edit itself leaves a valid IR, so the rejections above are about the names they write

cases.name: @http(name:) with an empty name
cases.schema:
entity Book { id: ID }
query book(id: ID @http(name: "")): Book?

cases.name: @http(name:) with a name that is not a string
cases.schema:
entity Book { id: ID }
query book(id: ID @http(name: 5)): Book?

cases.name: @http(name:) with a second argument
cases.schema:
entity Book { id: ID }
query book(id: ID @http(name: "book-id", method: GET)): Book?

cases.name: @http(name:) on an entity field
cases.schema:
entity Book { id: ID title: String @http(name: "book-title") }
query book(id: ID): Book?
cases.why: a wire name renames something a client sends; a result field keeps its schema name

cases.name: @http(name:) on a field's argument
guard: @http(name:) on an operation argument and an input field
a wire name that is another argument's name
cases.schema:
entity Book { id: ID }
query book(id: ID, q: String @http(name: "id")): Book?
cases.why: a binding reading `id` could not tell which argument the client meant

cases.name: two arguments with one wire name
cases.schema:
entity Book { id: ID }
query book(id: ID, a: String @http(name: "x"), b: String @http(name: "x")): Book?

cases.name: a wire name that is another input field's name
guard: a wire name equal to its own member's name, and one wire name in two operations
cases.why: the rule is about another member of the same owner; a member may be bound under its own name, and two operations are two scopes

cases.name: a block string holding its own fence
cases.why: \""" is the one escape; a lexer without it ends the description at the escaped fence and fails on what follows

cases.name: a description ending in a quote
cases.schema:
"""
say "hi"
"""
entity Book { id: ID }
query book(id: ID): Book?
cases.why: written on its own lines, the closing quote of the text is not read as part of the fence

cases.name: a description with LF line breaks
cases.schema:
entity Book {
  id: ID
  """
  line one
  line two
  """
  title: String
}
query book(id: ID): Book?

cases.name: the same description with CRLF line breaks
cases.schema:
entity Book {
  id: ID
  """
  line one
  line two
  """
  title: String
}
query book(id: ID): Book?
cases.sameAs: a description with LF line breaks
cases.why: a file saved on Windows is the same schema; a carriage return left in the text gives it another hash

cases.name: an object literal with name keys
the same literal with its keys quoted
cases.sameAs: an object literal with name keys

cases.name: an object key that is not a name
cases.schema:
entity Book { id: ID }
query book(id: ID, h: JSON = { "content-type": "text/plain" }): Book?
